subject: Day 43: bat toward a toy
bodyText:
Today's focus
Visually guided swiping is beginning: Avi is starting to look at an object and move his arm toward it. Week 7 keeps the focus on motor and sensory practice as nighttime stretches sometimes lengthen to 4-5 hours.

Action items
- Hold a lightweight toy within arm's reach and let Avi look at and bat toward it. Early swiping links his sharpening vision to arm movement and lays groundwork for deliberate reaching. AAP HealthyChildren: movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx
- Keep tummy-time bouts short and frequent after feeds, aiming for 30-45 minutes cumulative. Distributing it across the day reduces protest while still building upper-body strength. AAP HealthyChildren: tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Continue Avi's 400 IU/day vitamin D, and keep him in shade rather than direct sun during any outdoor time. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Varied cooing and gurgling, and brief startles that settle quickly, are signs of an organizing nervous system this week.
- [monitor] Movement that consistently favors one side, or a head that keeps turning to the same side, which can point to torticollis worth raising at the 2-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting past 24 hours, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row despite hunger cues.
- [call now] A rectal temperature of 100.4F (38.0C) or higher in an infant under 3 months, blue color around the lips, or labored breathing. For blue lips or an unresponsive spell, call 911 now!

Enrichment opportunities
- Live-sing a clapping song, shifting tempo from slow to fast and back, to keep Avi's perceptual range wide while his ear for rhythm sharpens. PubMed: infant music perception: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Lay Avi on a blanket on the grass in shade for a short window of outdoor light and varied texture, alternating with prone time on the blanket. AAP HealthyChildren: Vitamin D: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/healthy-living/nutrition/Pages/Vitamin-D-On-the-Double.aspx
- Offer a high-contrast object at arm's length and watch Avi fix on it and swipe. Pairing the visual target with the reach trains hand-eye coordination at its earliest stage. AAP HealthyChildren: movement: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-Birth-to-Three-Months.aspx

Upcoming
- Day 56-70 (Jul 6-20): 2-month well visit; vaccines due are HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, and IPV #1.
- Day 57-72 (Jul 7-22): the 24-48h post-vaccine window, when low-grade fever, drowsiness, and fussiness are expected.
- Day 84-91 (early August): the sleep consolidation window opens near 3 months.
- Day 112-126 (Aug 31-Sep 14): 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
